question.problem:
Evaluate
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡y}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.$

*Hint: First change the order of integration to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.$*
question.worked_solution:
We wish to find the limits of integration such that our integral can be expressed as 

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z.
$$

From the repeated integral, we see that the domain of integration $R$ can be written as a type II region as follows:

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\,\operatorname{arcsin}⁡y\le z\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,\,0\le x\le \operatorname{cos}⁡z\}
$$

Since all repeated integrals first integrate with respect to $x,$ the $x$-limits remain the same as before:

$$
{\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{{v}_{1}(z)}^{{v}_{2}(z)}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z
$$

 

Now, we consider the projection $D$ of $R$ onto the $yz$-plane shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/ed7308cf6c77f5d89b94ec90237fa9161fc85429182813f38b55d916bdbdaeef.png)

The region $D$ is type I region in the $yz$-plane:

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\operatorname{arcsin}⁡y\le z\le \frac{\pi }{2}\}.
$$

To change the order of integration from $\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y$ to $\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z,$ we write $D$ as a type II region.

Notice that the left boundary of the region $D$ is

$$
y=0
$$

and the right boundary of the region $D,$ written in the form $y=y(z),$ is

$$
z=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡y\,⟹\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡z.
$$

Then, the type II representation of the region is

$$
D=\{(y,z)\,:\,0\le z\le \frac{\pi }{2},\,0\le y\le \operatorname{sin}⁡z\},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14234808/assets/4fb3323b2c295df8351910890f20266840b131a4dfd8a7bba0d61a3eb03bea23.png)

Therefore, by swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{\operatorname{arcsin}⁡y}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡z}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡z}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡z}[\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡z}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}\text{d}x]\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡z}\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡z}\,[x]_{0}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡z}\operatorname{cos}⁡z\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡z}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[\operatorname{cos}⁡z\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡z}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡z}\text{d}y]\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡z\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡z}\,[y]_{0}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡z}\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{sin}⁡z\operatorname{cos}⁡z\sqrt{1+{cos}^{2}⁡z}\,\text{d}z \\  & ={[-\frac{1}{3}{(1+{cos}^{2}⁡z)}^{3/2}]}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}[(1+0)^{3/2}-(1+1)^{3/2}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}(1-{2}^{3/2}) \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{2}-1}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
